title: Decode One Instruction: JE rel8
blurb:
Windows x86-64.

At address 0x00007FF6A1B2C050, the raw bytes are:

74 F6

Decode this instruction fully: mnemonic, operand, how the operand is encoded, and the exact target address.

Answer: JE 0x00007FF6A1B2C048

0x74 is the one-byte short-form opcode for JE/JZ (jump if ZF=1). 0xF6 is a signed 8-bit relative displacement: 0xF6 = -10. The target is computed from the address of the NEXT instruction (current address + instruction length, here 2 bytes): next_rip = 0x00007FF6A1B2C052, so target = 0x00007FF6A1B2C052 + (-10) = 0x00007FF6A1B2C048. Since the displacement is negative, this is a backward branch, i.e. a classic bottom-of-loop jump back to the top; short Jcc opcodes (0x70-0x7F) only reach +/-127 bytes, farther targets need the two-byte 0x0F 8x near-jump form with a 32-bit displacement.
